compound.name: menthofuran
compound.one_liner: Minor peppermint oil constituent (1-8 %) and hepatotoxic metabolite of pulegone; limited together with pulegone by EMA.

identity.note: Stereo-unspecified record. KNApSAcK lists the peppermint form as (+)-menthofuran, CAS 17957-94-7.

occurrences.source_citation: EMA/HMPC. Assessment report on Mentha x piperita L., folium and aetheroleum, Rev. 1. EMA/HMPC/522409/2013 (15 Jan 2020). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/herbal-report/assessment-report-mentha-x-piperita-l-folium-and-aetheroleum-revision-1_en.pdf
occurrences.database: Dr. Duke's Phytochemical and Ethnobotanical Databases
occurrences.note: Duke: MENTHOFURAN Plant 0-2800 ppm. KNApSAcK lists (+)-menthofuran (C00003049) for Mentha piperita. EMA report has no statement on young leaves / early harvest. | Basis as recorded: % of essential oil (Ph. Eur. range) | The curation claim 'higher in young leaves / early-season oil' is removed (unsourced).

pharmacology.mechanism: Menthofuran is a major metabolite of pulegone; both cause similar hepatotoxicity in rodents, requiring bioactivation (CYP2E1, CYP1A2, CYP2C19 involved) with glutathione depletion [3].

evidence.claim: Menthofuran is hepatotoxic in rodents after bioactivation.
evidence.test_article_detail: menthofuran / pulegone (rodent data summarised by EMA)
evidence.outcome_summary: Liver (and kidney) are the target organs; toxicity qualitatively similar to pulegone.

processing_stability.volatility: steam-volatile: recovered in hydro/steam-distilled essential oil (see occurrence sources)
processing_stability.note: Solubility and heat-stability values not sourced in this pass.

safety_flags.detail: Counted together with pulegone against the EMA limit.
safety_flags.threshold_or_limit: pulegone + menthofuran 0.75 mg/kg bw/day (37.5 mg/person/day) lifelong; 75 mg/day for use under 1 year
safety_flags.source_citation: EMA/HMPC public statement on pulegone and menthofuran, EMA/HMPC/138386/2005 Rev.1 (2016)

compound.teaching_note: Menthofuran shows a plant making a compound the liver would also make: it is both an oil constituent and the metabolite of pulegone [3].
gaps: Claim that menthofuran is higher in young leaves / early-season oil removed: no source found (EMA reports and public statement silent) [3, 6].
No human evidence for the isolated compound found in this pass.
